evals.prompt: review this Ansible task file for best-practice violations: evals/files/review/tasks.yml
evals.expected_output: All four planted violations are caught: the unnamed shell package-install task, the status command without changed_when, the templated when clause, and the non-idempotent echo-append.
expectations: The first task is flagged on multiple counts: it has no name, it uses shell for a package install where the apt/package module exists, and it does not use an FQCN
The systemctl is-active status check is corrected with changed_when: false (or explicitly reported as always reporting changed)
The when: "{{ enable_tls }}" clause is corrected to a bare expression without Jinja2 braces (such as enable_tls | bool)
The echo-append shell task is replaced with, or flagged for, ansible.builtin.lineinfile as the idempotent alternative
No correct constructs are reported as violations — the lineinfile TLS task's module usage itself is not flagged

evals.prompt: Every run of my Ansible playbook restarts the app service, because I have a restart task right after the template task that writes its config. How do I refactor this so it only restarts when the config actually changed?
evals.expected_output: The restart moves into a handler that the template task notifies, so the service restarts only on config change and repeat runs stay quiet.
expectations: The solution moves the service restart into a handler and has the template task notify it
In the resulting design, the service restarts only when the template task reports changed, and a repeat run with an unchanged config triggers no restart
The handler and notification are shown with FQCN module usage (ansible.builtin.service or equivalent)
